Boris: Did you enjoy your lunch?
Adam: Yes. Your Workplace Health Program is very effective. Everything was healthy and delicious!
Boris: Ever since we started that program, people have been congratulating the kitchen staff. Now we'll do a little walk-about to meet some of your co-workers.
Kristi: Great! I would love to meet our new colleagues.

Boris: Let's start with the content team. Many of our authors are freelancers. They will be working from home for the rest of the week. We do have full-time journalists who have been working on different projects. In the future, they will be doing research for a large volume such as a dictionary. This is Janice Truman.
Janice: Hello. Welcome to Books for People.
Adam: Pleased to meet you, Ms. Truman. I'm Adam and this is Kristi.
Kristi: Hi!
Janice: You have both graduated in communications, right?
Kristi: Yes, that's right. We met while we were taking a class in journalism.
Janice: Excellent. You will be tackling your own writing projects in no time.

Adam: Great! We have been hoping to have that opportunity.
Boris: We can go in this room as soon as the marketing staff has finished their meeting. We have been marketing our products in a variety of ways. For example, Julian here will have soon finished a project promoting our books to educational institutions directly.
Julian: Hi.
Kristi: Hello!
Boris: Some people in this department have specialized in online marketing. Others have been working in more traditional channels. We noticed a significant increase in sales as soon as the subway ad campaign started.
Adam: It's a natural connection. People like to read on the subway.
Boris: Our in-house illustrators and graphic designers work here. It's very a hip office, as you can see from the art on the wall. You will be spending a lot of time with them.
Kristi: I'm looking forward to it!

The Present Perfect Continuous Tense
The Present Perfect Continuous is used to talk about actions that started in the past and have continued up until the present and the duration of those events is presented.

Example:
I've been calling you for an hour!
We have been hoping to have the opportunity to write articles.
We have been marketing our products in a variety of ways.
Other people have been working in more traditional channels.

The Present Perfect Continuous is also used when an action has been performed repeatedly or has been in progress.

Example:
I have been reading this book and I think it is quite interesting.
The Future Perfect Continuous Tense
The Future Perfect Continuous is used to talk about an action that started before a certain time in the future, and will continue up (action in progress) until that point in the future.

It refers to events or actions in progress in a time between now and some future time. It is most often used with a time expression.
Like other continuous tenses, the Future Perfect Continuous tense shows that an action or event continues.

For example:

You will have been waiting for almost an hour when the plane finally arrives.
Jason will have been teaching at the university for more than a year by the time he leaves for Europe.

The structure of the Future Perfect Continuous tense is:

subject + will + have + been + v-ing
Julian will have soon finished a project promoting our books to educational institutions.
You will have written your own article in no time.
